requirements.quote:
When a client first connects to a server, it is REQUIRED to send the
   ClientHello as its first TLS message.
requirements.condition: a client first connects to a server
requirements.required_behavior: send ClientHello as the first TLS message
requirements.forbidden_behavior: send another TLS message before ClientHello
requirements.why_checkable: The client's initial outbound TLS message can be observed in a connection trace.

requirements.quote:
The client will also send a
   ClientHello when the server has responded to its ClientHello with a
   HelloRetryRequest.
requirements.condition: the server responds to ClientHello with HelloRetryRequest
requirements.required_behavior: send another ClientHello
requirements.forbidden_behavior: continue the handshake without a retry ClientHello
requirements.why_checkable: The outbound transition after HelloRetryRequest can be checked for a second ClientHello.

requirements.quote:
In that case, the client MUST send the same
   ClientHello without modification, except as follows:
requirements.condition: the client sends ClientHello in response to HelloRetryRequest
requirements.required_behavior: preserve the original ClientHello except for the specifically allowed retry modifications
requirements.forbidden_behavior: make any unpermitted modification to the retry ClientHello
requirements.why_checkable: The initial and retry ClientHello messages can be structurally compared field by field.

requirements.quote:
If a "key_share" extension was supplied in the HelloRetryRequest,
      replacing the list of shares with a list containing a single
      KeyShareEntry from the indicated group.
requirements.condition: HelloRetryRequest supplies a key_share extension
requirements.required_behavior: replace the ClientHello key-share list with exactly one KeyShareEntry from the indicated group
requirements.forbidden_behavior: retain multiple shares or use a share from a different group
requirements.why_checkable: The retry ClientHello key_share vector can be checked for cardinality one and the requested group.

requirements.quote:
Removing the "early_data" extension (Section 4.2.10) if one was
      present.
requirements.condition: the initial ClientHello contained early_data and the server sent HelloRetryRequest
requirements.required_behavior: remove the early_data extension from the retry ClientHello
requirements.forbidden_behavior: retain early_data in the retry ClientHello
requirements.why_checkable: The retry ClientHello can be inspected for absence of the previously present extension.

requirements.quote: Early data is not permitted after a HelloRetryRequest.
requirements.condition: a HelloRetryRequest has been sent or received
requirements.required_behavior: disable early-data use for the remainder of that handshake
requirements.forbidden_behavior: send or accept early data after HelloRetryRequest
requirements.why_checkable: The connection state and record flow can be tested to ensure 0-RTT is no longer used after retry.

requirements.quote:
Including a "cookie" extension if one was provided in the
      HelloRetryRequest.
requirements.condition: HelloRetryRequest provides a cookie extension
requirements.required_behavior: include a cookie extension in the retry ClientHello
requirements.forbidden_behavior: omit the provided cookie from the retry ClientHello
requirements.why_checkable: The HelloRetryRequest and retry ClientHello extension lists can be compared for cookie propagation.

requirements.quote:
Updating the "pre_shared_key" extension if present by recomputing
      the "obfuscated_ticket_age" and binder values
requirements.condition: the retry ClientHello contains pre_shared_key
requirements.required_behavior: recompute each applicable obfuscated_ticket_age for the retry ClientHello
requirements.forbidden_behavior: reuse stale obfuscated_ticket_age values without recomputation
requirements.why_checkable: Ticket ages in the retry offer can be recomputed from the ticket metadata and retry time.

requirements.quote:
Updating the "pre_shared_key" extension if present by recomputing
      the "obfuscated_ticket_age" and binder values
requirements.condition: the retry ClientHello contains pre_shared_key
requirements.required_behavior: recompute the PSK binder values over the retry ClientHello
requirements.forbidden_behavior: reuse binders computed for the initial ClientHello
requirements.why_checkable: The retry binders can be independently derived from the retry transcript and compared.

requirements.quote:
(optionally)
      removing any PSKs which are incompatible with the server's
      indicated cipher suite.
requirements.condition: a PSK is incompatible with the cipher suite indicated by the server
requirements.required_behavior: permit that PSK to be removed from the retry ClientHello
requirements.forbidden_behavior: treat removal of an incompatible PSK as a forbidden retry modification
requirements.why_checkable: A retry-ClientHello consistency checker can explicitly allow removal only for incompatible PSKs.

requirements.quote:
Optionally adding, removing, or changing the length of the
      "padding" extension [RFC7685].
requirements.condition: the client constructs a retry ClientHello
requirements.required_behavior: permit padding to be added, removed, or changed in length
requirements.forbidden_behavior: treat those padding-only differences as forbidden retry modifications
requirements.why_checkable: The comparison logic can be tested with each of the explicitly allowed padding differences.

requirements.quote:
Other modifications that may be allowed by an extension defined in
      the future and present in the HelloRetryRequest.
requirements.condition: an implemented future extension is present in HelloRetryRequest and defines an additional retry-ClientHello modification
requirements.required_behavior: permit the modification authorized by that extension
requirements.forbidden_behavior: reject the modification solely because it is not one of the RFC 8446-defined retry changes
requirements.why_checkable: For an implemented future extension, retry comparison can be checked against its declared modification rule and presence in HelloRetryRequest.

requirements.quote:
Because TLS 1.3 forbids renegotiation, if a server has negotiated
   TLS 1.3 and receives a ClientHello at any other time, it MUST
   terminate the connection with an "unexpected_message" alert.
requirements.condition: a server that negotiated TLS 1.3 receives ClientHello outside the initial or HelloRetryRequest retry positions
requirements.required_behavior: terminate the connection
requirements.forbidden_behavior: perform TLS 1.3 renegotiation
requirements.why_checkable: An extra ClientHello can be injected after negotiation and the connection termination and alert observed.

requirements.quote:
If a server established a TLS connection with a previous version of
   TLS and receives a TLS 1.3 ClientHello in a renegotiation, it MUST
   retain the previous protocol version.
requirements.condition: a pre-TLS 1.3 connection receives a TLS 1.3 ClientHello during renegotiation
requirements.required_behavior: retain the connection's previous protocol version
requirements.forbidden_behavior: change the renegotiated connection to another protocol version
requirements.why_checkable: The negotiated version before and after a legacy renegotiation attempt can be compared.

requirements.quote:
In particular, it MUST NOT
   negotiate TLS 1.3.
requirements.condition: a pre-TLS 1.3 connection receives a TLS 1.3 ClientHello during renegotiation
requirements.required_behavior: continue using the prior-version renegotiation rules
requirements.forbidden_behavior: negotiate TLS 1.3
requirements.why_checkable: A version assertion can verify that renegotiation never upgrades the connection to TLS 1.3.

requirements.condition: when encoding or parsing ClientHello
requirements.required_behavior: use the declared field order: legacy_version, random, legacy_session_id, cipher_suites, legacy_compression_methods, then extensions
requirements.forbidden_behavior: reorder the declared ClientHello fields
requirements.why_checkable: The serializer and parser layouts can be compared with the declared field sequence.

requirements.quote: uint16 ProtocolVersion;
requirements.condition: when encoding or parsing a ProtocolVersion value
requirements.required_behavior: represent ProtocolVersion as an unsigned 16-bit value
requirements.forbidden_behavior: encode ProtocolVersion with a different width
requirements.why_checkable: The wire codec's ProtocolVersion width is directly testable.

requirements.quote: uint8 CipherSuite[2];    /* Cryptographic suite selector */
requirements.condition: when encoding or parsing a CipherSuite selector
requirements.required_behavior: represent CipherSuite as exactly two bytes
requirements.forbidden_behavior: encode a CipherSuite selector with a different length
requirements.why_checkable: Encoded cipher-suite selectors can be checked for their fixed two-byte width.

requirements.quote: opaque legacy_session_id<0..32>;
requirements.condition: when encoding or parsing ClientHello.legacy_session_id
requirements.required_behavior: encode a variable-length opaque value from 0 through 32 bytes
requirements.forbidden_behavior: encode legacy_session_id longer than 32 bytes
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary encodings at 0, 32, and above 32 bytes can be tested.

requirements.quote: CipherSuite cipher_suites<2..2^16-2>;
requirements.condition: when encoding or parsing ClientHello.cipher_suites
requirements.required_behavior: encode a CipherSuite vector whose byte length is from 2 through 2^16-2
requirements.forbidden_behavior: encode an empty, odd-sized, or oversized cipher_suites vector
requirements.why_checkable: The vector length prefix and two-byte element alignment can be checked at the declared bounds.

requirements.quote: Extension extensions<8..2^16-1>;
requirements.condition: when encoding or parsing ClientHello.extensions
requirements.required_behavior: encode an Extension vector whose byte length is from 8 through 2^16-1
requirements.forbidden_behavior: encode the ClientHello extensions vector outside the declared bounds
requirements.why_checkable: The extensions vector's length prefix can be tested against the lower and upper bounds.

requirements.quote:
In
      TLS 1.3, the client indicates its version preferences in the
      "supported_versions" extension (Section 4.2.1) and the
      legacy_version field MUST be set to 0x0303
requirements.condition: the client constructs a TLS 1.3 ClientHello
requirements.required_behavior: set legacy_version to 0x0303
requirements.forbidden_behavior: put another version value in legacy_version
requirements.why_checkable: The fixed legacy_version bytes can be read directly from ClientHello.

requirements.quote:
TLS 1.3 ClientHellos are identified as having
      a legacy_version of 0x0303 and a supported_versions extension
      present with 0x0304 as the highest version indicated therein.
requirements.condition: an implementation identifies a ClientHello as TLS 1.3
requirements.required_behavior: require a supported_versions extension to be present
requirements.forbidden_behavior: identify a ClientHello without supported_versions as TLS 1.3
requirements.why_checkable: The version-classification branch can be tested with and without the extension.

requirements.quote:
TLS 1.3 ClientHellos are identified as having
      a legacy_version of 0x0303 and a supported_versions extension
      present with 0x0304 as the highest version indicated therein.
requirements.condition: an implementation identifies a ClientHello as TLS 1.3
requirements.required_behavior: require 0x0304 to be the highest version in supported_versions
requirements.forbidden_behavior: identify the message as TLS 1.3 when supported_versions does not indicate 0x0304 as highest
requirements.why_checkable: The classifier can compare the highest offered version with the fixed TLS 1.3 value.

requirements.quote: random:  32 bytes generated by a secure random number generator.
requirements.condition: the client generates ClientHello.random
requirements.required_behavior: produce exactly 32 bytes
requirements.forbidden_behavior: use a random field of another length
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded random field has a fixed observable length.

requirements.quote: random:  32 bytes generated by a secure random number generator.
requirements.condition: the client generates ClientHello.random
requirements.required_behavior: generate the bytes with a secure random number generator
requirements.forbidden_behavior: use a deterministic or non-secure source for ClientHello.random
requirements.why_checkable: The random-generation call path and its cryptographic RNG dependency can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
A client which has a
      cached session ID set by a pre-TLS 1.3 server SHOULD set this
      field to that value.
requirements.condition: the client has a cached session ID set by a pre-TLS 1.3 server
requirements.required_behavior: set legacy_session_id to the cached value
requirements.why_checkable: A client with a seeded legacy session cache can be checked for echoing the cached value.

requirements.quote:
In compatibility mode (see Appendix D.4),
      this field MUST be non-empty
requirements.condition: the client operates in compatibility mode
requirements.required_behavior: make legacy_session_id non-empty
requirements.forbidden_behavior: send a zero-length legacy_session_id
requirements.why_checkable: Compatibility-mode ClientHello messages can be checked for a nonzero session ID length.

requirements.quote:
so a client not offering a
      pre-TLS 1.3 session MUST generate a new 32-byte value.
requirements.condition: the client is in compatibility mode and is not offering a pre-TLS 1.3 session
requirements.required_behavior: generate a new 32-byte legacy_session_id
requirements.forbidden_behavior: reuse an old value or generate a value of another length
requirements.why_checkable: Repeated compatibility-mode connections without a legacy session can be checked for fresh 32-byte values.

requirements.quote:
This value
      need not be random but SHOULD be unpredictable
requirements.condition: the client generates a compatibility-mode legacy_session_id
requirements.required_behavior: make the value unpredictable
requirements.forbidden_behavior: fixate on a predictable constant value
requirements.why_checkable: The value-generation implementation can be inspected for an unpredictable source rather than a constant.

requirements.quote:
Otherwise, it MUST be set as a zero-length vector
      (i.e., a zero-valued single byte length field).
requirements.condition: the client is not using the compatibility-mode non-empty legacy_session_id behavior
requirements.required_behavior: encode legacy_session_id as a zero-length vector with a zero-valued one-byte length field
requirements.forbidden_behavior: include session ID bytes
requirements.why_checkable: The vector length byte and absence of value bytes can be inspected directly.

requirements.quote:
cipher_suites:  A list of the symmetric cipher options supported by
      the client, specifically the record protection algorithm
      (including secret key length) and a hash to be used with HKDF
requirements.condition: the client constructs ClientHello.cipher_suites
requirements.required_behavior: list supported record-protection algorithm and HKDF-hash pairs
requirements.forbidden_behavior: advertise a pair the client does not support
requirements.why_checkable: The advertised pairs can be compared with the client's enabled cipher and hash implementations.

requirements.quote:
in
      descending order of client preference.
requirements.condition: the client encodes more than one cipher suite
requirements.required_behavior: order cipher_suites in descending client preference
requirements.forbidden_behavior: encode the list in an order inconsistent with the client's preference order
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted list can be compared with the configured preference ranking.

requirements.quote:
If the list contains cipher suites that the server
      does not recognize, support, or wish to use, the server MUST
      ignore those cipher suites
requirements.condition: ClientHello.cipher_suites contains a suite the server does not recognize, support, or wish to use
requirements.required_behavior: ignore that cipher suite
requirements.forbidden_behavior: select the unusable suite or fail solely because it is present when usable entries remain
requirements.why_checkable: An unknown or disabled suite can be placed alongside a supported suite to test selection behavior.

requirements.quote:
and process the remaining ones as
      usual.
requirements.condition: the server has ignored unrecognized, unsupported, or unwanted cipher suites
requirements.required_behavior: continue normal processing of the remaining cipher suites
requirements.forbidden_behavior: discard or skip otherwise usable remaining entries
requirements.why_checkable: A mixed offer can verify that the server still negotiates from supported remaining entries.

requirements.quote:
If the client is attempting a PSK key establishment, it
      SHOULD advertise at least one cipher suite indicating a Hash
      associated with the PSK.
requirements.condition: the client attempts PSK key establishment
requirements.required_behavior: advertise at least one cipher suite whose Hash is associated with the PSK
requirements.why_checkable: The PSK hash can be compared with the hashes of all offered cipher suites.

requirements.quote:
For every TLS 1.3 ClientHello, this vector
      MUST contain exactly one byte, set to zero
requirements.condition: encoding or parsing a TLS 1.3 ClientHello
requirements.required_behavior: encode legacy_compression_methods as exactly one byte whose value is zero
requirements.forbidden_behavior: use another vector length or byte value
requirements.why_checkable: The vector length and sole byte can be checked directly on the wire.

requirements.quote:
If a
      TLS 1.3 ClientHello is received with any other value in this
      field, the server MUST abort the handshake with an
      "illegal_parameter" alert.
requirements.condition: a server receives a TLS 1.3 ClientHello whose legacy_compression_methods is not exactly the required zero byte
requirements.required_behavior: abort the handshake
requirements.forbidden_behavior: accept the malformed legacy compression field
requirements.why_checkable: Malformed vector lengths and nonzero values can be injected to observe the required alert.

requirements.quote:
TLS 1.3 servers might
      receive TLS 1.2 or prior ClientHellos which contain other
      compression methods and (if negotiating such a prior version) MUST
      follow the procedures for the appropriate prior version of TLS.
requirements.condition: a TLS 1.3-capable server receives a legacy ClientHello and negotiates TLS 1.2 or earlier
requirements.required_behavior: process compression methods using the procedures for the negotiated prior TLS version
requirements.forbidden_behavior: apply the TLS 1.3 zero-only rule to the negotiated prior-version handshake
requirements.why_checkable: Legacy ClientHello handling can be tested under a prior-version negotiation path.
